Frankfurt, 1608 · Clavis, printed pp. 56–57

Modus II: from printed letters to German

Follow one worked example from the printed page through transcription and extraction to a mechanically recomputed plaintext. Every visual has an equivalent table or prose account.

Where the print disagrees. The 41 printed letters and the 45-letter normalized German agree in their first five decoded positions. At six, both the cipher line and the cover word bene give b. The key turns b into d. The German has t. The printed sources disagree here. Their wording does not establish how the difference arose.

1. Printed example

Printed evidence

Intentio Ich bitte dich komm von stund an zu mir/ es thut sehr noth.

English I beg you, come to me at once; it is very urgent.

Plain-text account

The first five decoded letters agree with the German. At position six the list prints b, also the initial of bene. The pair db decodes it as d. The first t in bitte would require r under the pair tr. At position eight the letter list gives p and the eighth even cover word is gaudium, beginning with g. The page preserves both differences.

Provenance and limits
  • Frankfurt, 1608, Herzog August Bibliothek Wolfenbüttel, Fb 243. Printed p. 56 describes the shift and diagrams the circle. Printed p. 57 gives the paired alphabet, German intention, significant letters and cover.
  • AI visual collation of HAB Fb 243 on 23 November 2026 checked all 41 types in the significant-letter line, the 22 printed pairs, the German and the 85-word prayer. No human review is documented.
  • The public evidence register preserves exact crops of the letter line and prayer. The earlier 42-letter transcription is retained in the correction history.
